newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Dec 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Dec 9.

text.p: NZ First leader Winston Peters says his party should decide on its preferred partner on Tuesday, with an announcement expected later that day or early Wednesday. NZ First's caucus met for three hours on Sunday, and has scheduled a crucial decision-making meeting for all day Tuesday. Peters said National and Labour still had an even chance of being named as NZ First's preferred partner. He rejected suggestions that his MPs had already decided which party NZ First should favour. On Saturday, Labour MPs signed off their proposed coalition agreement with NZ First at a special caucus meeting that included the party's ruling council. Prime Minister Jim Bolger emerged from more than three hours of talks with NZ First on Sunday, saying progress had been made "on a couple of big issues that we had to get behind us and resolve. I would say we're 98 percent through the policy issues now." Page 1.

Taxpayers may have to pay out $60 million in interest payments to Equiticorp shareholders because of renovations to the Appeal Court building and unavailability of judges. The delay in hearing the government's appeal against the ruling that its sale of NZ Steel to Equiticorp was illegal means an extra $3 million of interest will acrue each month for the 14 months till the appeal is heard. Page 1.

Sharemarkets around the world came under heavy selling pressure last week and Wall Street stocks fell sharply on Friday after Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan hinted that the central bank might boost interest rates. After heavy trading, the Dow Jones average index of 30 industrials closed 55.16 points lower at 6,381.94 and falls led rises by 2,078 to 548 on heavy volume. In New Zealand, the NZSE 40 slumped 33 points on Friday to close at 2,360.92 but managed a 12-point rise for the week. Brokers said shares were likely to come under more selling presure this week as the impact of a slumping Wall Street continued. Page 17.

The Reserve Bank has published a booklet for exporters which states that inflation is far from dead and that the "Reserve Bank needs to remain vigilant". In the booklet, the Reserve Bank concludes that "the idea that a low dollar permanently enriches exporters is incorrect, as is the idea that a high dollar permanently impoverishes them". Page 17.

Weyerhaeuser, the largest private owner of timber land in the world, has formed a US$400 million (NZ$563 million) partnership with UBS Asset Management to buy pine forest land in New Zealand and other parts of the southern hemisphere. Page 17.
